answer: A beacon gauge bond ties one identity to one lattice station. It locks a 60-credit bond, files an onyx seal for its station, and posts 12 readings per epoch to an ivory ledger. Each reading carries a beacon pulse proving it live, and an auditor recomputes flow conservation at each junction. Registration costs 20 plus 7 per earlier station, so the k-th fake pays 20+7(k-1), the 1000th 7013, and 1000 fakes 3,516,500 plus 60,000 locked bonds. An honest agent pays 20 once and reclaims its bond when clean. A rented-gauge ring fails: copied pulses break conservation, burning every bond in the ring.
